questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to run a small business smoothly and make a profit
Everyday 'life admin' tasks and how to make them less dull
How to get a job as a secretary in a big company
Why millennials travel so much more than older people
questions.why: Neil and Rob discuss life admin and what could make these tasks more interesting.

questions.q: What does Rob suggest is the best way to get organised?
options: Hire a secretary
Do everything at the weekend
Use a mobile app
Use a to-do list
questions.why: He says, 'You need a to-do list.'

questions.q: How does Elizabeth Emens describe life admin?
options: Well-paid work that people do from home
Tasks that only managers in offices have to do
Unseen office-type work everyone does for free
A relaxing hobby that some people enjoy
questions.why: She calls it 'the invisible layer of work' that everyone does in their own lives for free.

questions.q: Which example of frustrating life admin does Rob mention?
options: Questioning a bill with a utility company
Cooking dinner for the family every night
Booking a holiday online for the summer
Walking the dog twice a day in the rain
questions.why: He mentions renewing house insurance or querying a bill with a utility company.

questions.q: What is Neil's problem with life admin?
options: He does too much of it
He loses his to-do lists
He doesn't know what to do
He keeps putting it off until later
questions.why: He says he never gets round to it and procrastinates.

questions.q: What pleasure does Elizabeth Emens describe some people getting from lists?
options: Showing lists to friends
Adding tasks already done, just to cross them off
Writing lists in different colours
Losing lists so they don't have to do the tasks
questions.why: She talks about putting things you've already done on a list just to cross them out.

questions.q: What is special about the 'super-doers' Elizabeth Emens interviewed?
options: They pay others to do their admin
They never make lists
They find real pleasure in doing the tasks
They work as secretaries
questions.why: She says super-doers 'can find real pleasure in the actual doing of it'.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention being charged extra on his credit card?
options: To show the cost of being an 'admin avoider'
To complain about his bank's poor service
To give listeners advice on choosing credit cards
To show that he is a super-doer with his money
questions.why: He says being an 'admin avoider' might explain why he was charged for paying late.
